cues.text: Okay Mary, I know I’m putting on weight with all my bad eating habits.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: That’s right. Chocolate bars, pizzas, and all washed down with litres of soft drink. And with all the sugar in soft drink, I think we can say you’re definitely overindulging, don’t you think?
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: I know, I know. I intend to definitely stop drinking that from now on.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: And that’s part of the sensible eating plan that we have agreed we need to formulate—one that we can both follow.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: That’s right, sensible, and practical — allowing us to indulge in some sweet foods on occasions.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: On rare occasions, and we’re going to cut out all the pizzas and hamburgers.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Well, not totally. I thought you said pizzas could be eaten once a week. You know how I like pizzas.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: No. I said once every two months. Once a week was ice cream, not pizza.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Yeah, that’s because you like ice cream. I prefer pizza.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Peter, if you want to lose weight, you need to be disciplined, in both what you eat, and what you do, which brings us to the issue of exercise.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: That’s right. So, jogging twice a week, and hiking on Saturdays, right?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: No, hiking is Sundays, allowing Saturdays for the light walking exercise. I’ve investigated, and discovered there are a lot of walking trails around this suburb, with many beautiful places if you just look around.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: So what’s happening this Saturday? A walk around the city?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: That’s later in the month. This Saturday we’ll visit Pine Park.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Hill Park is nicer, with great views, too.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Yes, but we have to travel too far to reach Hill Park, so I ruled that out, and I love the smell of pines.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: And what about the weekday meals? Salads every night, I suppose?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: No, it’s important to vary the meals so that the food remains interesting and fun. The only common factor is the fruit juice, but otherwise we’ll have a variety of healthy fare, from salads, to fish, to lean meat.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: I'd rather have meat every night, but you’re the boss.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: If you want to lose weight, you’ll have to accept this program, okay?
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Okay.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Now Mary, you said we could have a little treat in our diet plan three times a week: specifically, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Sundays.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Yes. A very small treat, but something to reward us for all the discipline shown. Such rewards will motivate us to continue the diet.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: So, on Tuesdays, what can I choose?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: You have a choice between a small serving of chocolate, ice cream, or biscuits.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Okay, well, I’ll go for the biscuits. I love those crunchy little things with my cup of tea. So do you, right?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: I do indeed, so I’ll have them, too, saving the ice cream for later.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: But I know how much you like ice cream, so why don’t you save it for the end of the week? That will give you the motivation to keep going, and you can have chocolate midweek?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: That’s a good idea, but I think the most important thing is for you and I to eat different things on those other two days.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Well, if you think that way, I’ll eat the ice cream on Thursdays, not the chocolate. Okay?
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Well, if you’re having that, then I can’t have ice cream. In order to be different, I’ll have the chocolate.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: So, we can compare our different snacks, and maybe even share a little with each other.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Exactly! And the variety and fun involved will take our minds of wanting more.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Eating for fun! A good idea!
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: And then you can have the chocolate on Sunday, right?
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: But I like biscuits? Actually, I want biscuits again—to have with my cup of tea.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: But you have the biscuits on Monday, remember, and we can’t repeat.
cues.speaker: Mary

cues.text: Ah come on! This isn’t fixed in concrete. I can have them again instead of chocolate. You might like variety, but I don’t. I’m a creature of habit.
cues.speaker: Peter

cues.text: Well, the whole point of this was to taste different snacks, but if you want the same thing, okay. I, for one, am sticking to the original plan, with ice cream to finish the week, and not another dose of chocolate.
cues.speaker: Mary
